correctness.rationale: For D chosen in both parts, set I={i:a_i in D}, J={j:b_j in D}; an omitted a_i has |J|-1_{i in J} selected neighbors and an omitted b_j has |I|-1_{j in I}. If a side is full, n>=3 forces the whole graph. Otherwise nonempty side-complements force |I|,|J| in {1,2}; (1,1) gives matched nonedge pair; mixed (1,2) impossible; (2,2) requires I union J=[n], possible only n=3,4, in exactly six ordered cases each. This yields n*x^2+6*x^4+x^{2n} for n=3,4 and n*x²+x^{2n} else. Independent direct subset enumeration for n=3..8 matched all coefficients, n=3..8 counts 10,11,6,7,8,9, and checked induced connectivity. General statement follows symbolically, not from enumerations.
residual_risks: Perfect domination here constrains only outside D; not efficient domination, which also constrains vertices in D. n=2 excluded, as disconnected.

originality.rationale: Nayaka et al 2021 defines perfect-domination polynomial and handles complete bipartite and other named families, but the crown is a matching-deleted K_{n,n}, not a direct specialization of that result; the n matching nonedge pairs and two n=3,4 exceptional layers require accounting for missing edges. Published Resultary restrained-domination and perfect-Roman results on crowns share minimum pairs but are different properties and do not imply the full all-size perfect-domination polynomial.
residual_risks: Complete Dalal–Johnson 2013 article not read; unknown whether an edge-deletion corollary already supplies this precise all-size polynomial. Unindexed crown perfect-domination formula could exist.

value.rationale: A complete all-cardinality polynomial and support classification for a natural standard graph family is a reproducible invariant useful for perfect-domination enumeration, not simply recomputation of a known K_n,n table. It identifies two sharp low-order exceptions and the exact connectedness threshold; these are natural structural facts even though the proof is short.
residual_risks: Easy family-specific closed form need not imply broad computational complexity results or analogous formulas for arbitrary bipartite graphs.

limitations: Applies only connected Cr_n, n>=3; standard outside-only perfect domination, not efficient/total or weighted alternatives; 2013 perturbation paper partly accessible.
